project_type: OMK (oh-my-kiro) framework — bash hooks + Python scripts + Markdown skills/commands/agents/templates/docs
build_system: No build step. Python uses pip; Markdown is consumed by hooks/skills directly.
test_framework: pytest (Python unit tests under tests/) + custom bash test scripts under tests/**/*.sh and tests/knowledge/run.sh
verification_instructions: 1) Diff sanity: `git diff --stat main` should show only .md files and only prose/heading changes; YAML front-matter, fenced code blocks, links, paths, and test-anchored phrases must remain identical. 2) Run pytest with the ignore set above and confirm pass count is unchanged from baseline (60 passed / 8 pre-existing failures). 3) Run bash sanity scripts: `bash tests/test-agents-template.sh` (must keep its 27 passing assertions), `bash tests/knowledge/run.sh` (must keep its passing scripts; do NOT regress the 5/9 baseline). 4) Spot-check 3 translated files for: front-matter intact, fenced code blocks intact, technical terms preserved (deploy/commit/push/pull request/endpoint/payload/token/middleware/runtime/framework/pipeline/webhook/API/SDK/IAM/JSON/YAML/AWS/Kiro/MCP/CDK/CloudFormation/Terraform/Docker), markdown structure (headings, lists, tables) identical in shape.
snapshot_or_generated_files: knowledge/.health-report.md is auto-generated by hooks/feedback/kb-health-report.sh. The current checked-in copy is a snapshot; translating the human prose (section titles like 'Status', 'Actions Needed') is fine and the regenerator will re-overwrite on the next hook run with the same English literals. Translate it but expect it to be re-overwritten. docs/plans/*.progress.md and docs/plans/*.findings.md are human-written iteration logs (not machine-generated); translate the prose, keep timestamps/paths/hashes.
setup_instructions: 1) `python3 -m pip install --quiet pytest` (already done in this sandbox). 2) Working directory is /projects/sandbox/oh-my-kiro on branch main with a clean tree.
environment_constraints: OPEN_INTERNET sandbox. Python 3.9 is installed; pytest installed via pip. Some pytest suites are pre-existing-broken on this checkout: test_generate_configs.py + tests/ralph-loop/test_{evaluator,pty_runner,ralph_loop}.py fail collection due to Python 3.10+ `X | None` syntax used in scripts/generate_configs.py and scripts/lib/, and test_debugging_skill.py references skills/debugging/SKILL.md which has been renamed to skills/omk-debugging/. Also pre-existing failing tests under tests/test_ov_*.py and tests/test_debug_hook_trigger.py rely on OpenViking sockets and hook environment that this sandbox does not have. These failures EXIST ON main BEFORE any translation. Bash test baselines on main: tests/test-agents-template.sh = 27 pass / 1 fail (pre-existing 'OMK SECTIONS' mismatch on coding.md), tests/test-init-project.sh = 1 pass / 9 fail (pre-existing — references files that don't exist), tests/instruction-guard/test-write-protection.sh = 3 pass / 5 fail (pre-existing), tests/knowledge/run.sh = 5/9 (l1-rules-injection + l1-corruption-recall are pre-existing failures due to context-enrichment.sh dedup). Translation must NOT regress these counts.
contribution_requirements: Per task spec: in-place translation, preserve YAML front-matter, fenced code blocks, inline code, URLs, paths, CLI commands, variable/function/parameter names, technical product/tool names (AWS, Kiro, MCP, CDK, CloudFormation, Terraform, Docker, etc.), consecrated tech terms left in English (deploy, commit, push, pull request, endpoint, payload, token, middleware, runtime, framework, pipeline, webhook, etc.), technical acronyms (API, SDK, IAM, VPC, DNS, HTTP, JSON, YAML, etc.). Translate explanatory prose, headings (keeping technical terms), narrative docs. Use 'você' (informal technical), professional tone. NO em dashes (—). Files already in Brazilian Portuguese must be skipped unchanged.
key_patterns: 1) Many files are mixed Chinese + English. The user's request is explicitly EN→PT-BR; Chinese passages stay in Chinese (do not translate CN→PT-BR). Each pure-Chinese file is to be SKIPPED unchanged per the 'already in Portuguese' rule generalized to 'not in English'. 2) Skill SKILL.md files have YAML front-matter with `name:`, `description:`, `argument-hint:`, `disable-model-invocation:`. Front-matter values may contain user-facing trigger keywords. The trigger phrases inside `description:` are matched at runtime by hooks/feedback/context-enrichment.sh against user prompts — so trigger keyword lists like 'write code', 'implement', 'fix this' inside `description:` MUST be preserved exactly (do not translate them, they are pattern-matched literals). The English narrative prose around them in the description is translatable, but the comma-separated trigger keyword tokens are not. To stay safe, keep the entire `description:` value verbatim. 3) `templates/agents-sections/*.md` contain HTML BEGIN/END markers (e.g. `<!-- BEGIN OMK PRINCIPLES -->`) and exact-match phrases that tests/test-agents-template.sh greps for: 'Evidence before claims' (principles.md), 'Explore' + 'Skill Routing' (workflow.md), 'episodes.md' (self-learning.md), 'Authority Matrix' (authority.md). Must preserve the literal English phrases. The body of these templates is mostly Chinese (skip CN parts); the few English bullet keywords are test-anchored. 4) `templates/agents-types/coding.md` must contain 'Coding agent' literal (tests/test-init-project.sh:65), 'OMK SECTIONS' literal (tests/test-agents-template.sh). `templates/agents-types/gtm.md` must contain 'GTM'. 5) `tests/knowledge/fixtures/{episodes-healthy,rules-healthy,rules-corrupted}.md` are TEST FIXTURES — l1-corruption-recall.sh and l1-rules-injection.sh grep for exact substrings ('JSON = jq', 'sed.*JSON', 'stat -f', 'Skill 文件不得', 'read/write/shell', 'testword'). DO NOT modify these files. 6) Front-matter of a SKILL.md uses YAML; preserve indentation and quoting style exactly.
relevant_files: tests/knowledge/fixtures/*.md (DO NOT TRANSLATE — fixtures asserted by tests)
directory_structure: agents/=subagent prompts; commands/=user-triggered command markdowns; docs/INDEX.md+docs/EXTENSION-GUIDE.md+docs/e2e-report*.md+docs/designs/+docs/plans/+docs/releases/=user-facing docs; knowledge/=runtime knowledge base (episodes, rules, archive, reference, INDEX); skills/=skill definitions with front-matter and SKILL.md; templates/=scaffolding copied by tools/init-project.sh; tests/knowledge/fixtures/=test fixtures (do NOT touch); .kiro/rules/=steering rules read by Kiro at runtime.
